camps.name: Meany Crest
camps.why: The usual overnight for this climb: flat wind-walled sites above Summerland, meltwater on the nearby glacier, and a start that is short enough for one night.

camps.name: Summerland Camp
camps.why: Easier and more sheltered, with running water, but about 1,600 ft lower, so summit day gets much longer. Used by parties that arrive late or stop short.

camps.name: Toe of the Fryingpan Glacier
camps.why: A higher, colder bivy on moraine at the glacier edge. It saves a little time on summit morning but has less shelter than Meany Crest.

camps.name: Whitman Glacier notch camp
camps.why: The highest sites, in the gap between the two glaciers, make summit day short. Expect wind and cold, and a long carry to get there, so few parties choose it.

plan_conflict: The plan puts the night at about 7,900 ft near Whitman Crest, but parties report sleeping on the Meany Crest bench near 7,500 ft; Summerland was on file as a second main.

camps.name: Avalanche Glacier high bivy
camps.why: Placing camp high on the ridge beside the glacier shortens summit day; the plan assumes this is where both nights are spent.

camps.name: Cold Springs / South Climb trailhead
camps.why: A trailhead camp the night before an early start, not slept at on the plan's nights. It costs nothing in carrying but adds a full day of approach.

camps.name: Lunch Counter
camps.why: The South Climb high camp, on a different side of the mountain; relevant only to parties who descend that way instead of returning to the glacier camp.

camps.name: Morrison Creek Campground
camps.why: A fallback car campground below the trailhead when the upper road is too rough or Cold Springs is full; it adds miles to the approach.

plan_conflict: The plan names Mad Cat Meadow or Salt Creek for the night, but neither is on file, and no source on this route's camps was found; the high bivy is assumed.

camps.name: High Camp (Adams Creek Meadows)
camps.why: The north-side base: about three hours from the trailhead, meadow ground with snowmelt water, and the ridge starts straight above. Exposed to wind.

camps.name: Adams Glacier moraine bivy
camps.why: Rock sites on the moraine and by the lake at the foot of the glacier cut the summit-day distance, but they are smaller, less sheltered and shift year to year.

camps.name: High Camp (Adams Creek Meadows)
camps.why: The standard base for the north side, a short carry from the trailhead and directly below the glacier. Snowmelt is the only water, and the site is windy.

camps.name: Adams Glacier moraine bivy
camps.why: Moving up onto the moraine shaves distance off the icefall start, but sites are small and exposed and change as the glacier retreats.

camps.name: High Camp (Adams Creek Meadows)
camps.why: Where north-side parties sleep: a three-hour carry from Killen Creek, snowmelt water, and the lava fields and glacier reached in the morning. Very windy.

camps.name: High Camp (Adams Creek Meadows)
camps.why: The north-side base for the summit day: a three-hour carry, snowmelt water and an hour's traverse to the glacier. Exposed to wind, and you return to it after the climb.

camps.name: Sunrise Camp
camps.why: The established high camp at the edge of the glacier: snow-free ground, close to the route, and the summit day returns to it before the walk out.

plan_conflict: Many parties pack up and hike out the afternoon of summit day, so night 2 is often skipped; the plan still lists it.

camps.name: High Camp (Adams Creek Meadows)
camps.why: The base for the north side: about three hours in, snowmelt water, and the ridge starts above. The summit day returns here, so it is the second night too.

camps.name: High Camp (Adams Creek Meadows)
camps.why: The north-side base, about three hours from the trailhead, with snowmelt water and the ridge starting above. Windy, so pitch behind rocks.

camps.name: Adams Glacier moraine bivy
camps.why: Rock bivy sites on the way up the ridge and by the lake below the glacier shorten summit day, but offer less room and shelter than High Camp.

camps.name: The Lunch Counter
camps.why: The standard high camp: rock windbreaks already built, snow to melt, and summit day starts above it. Often windy and crowded; carry water early season.

camps.name: Morrison Creek drainage
camps.why: A quieter, lower alternative with water, but it adds elevation to the summit day. Also used by parties arriving late who skip the rough road.

camps.name: Avalanche Valley
camps.why: The only established camp near the Wilson and Rusk glaciers: meadow ground with creeks and ponds. Reaching it is a long off-trail day, so expect a tired start.

camps.name: Cold Springs / South Climb trailhead
camps.why: The trailhead where this plan starts and ends; a car camp here the night before saves nothing on night 1 but gives an earlier start.
